biggestGap: Every square joint is a blown-out white glowing hairline, so the marble field reads as a wireframe grid laid over stone; in the film the joints are the DARKEST thing on the board — recessed grooves carrying a beaded inlay band that reads as a row of fine dark dentils — and no joint anywhere in the reference is brighter than the square beside it.
critiqueDetail: Blind pair called correctly with no hesitation: A is the render, B is the film, high confidence. Real progress on the round-3 gap — the light squares now carry genuine ink-black branching veins and there is a real cream-vs-navy value split, and faint vertical smears under the plinths show reflection is finally switched on. But the fix introduced a worse artifact. At 2x on the mid-field every single square boundary in the render is a hard 1px near-white line, uniform brightness from the near kerb to the back rank, running straight through both light and dark squares. Crop the film at the same place and the joints are the opposite polarity: dark recessed grooves, and running along them a fine beaded/dentil inlay band that also reads dark. Nothing on the film board is a bright hairline. This alone makes A read as CG geometry with an emissive UV seam. Two supporting failures. First, colour temperature on the marble: meanLitHueDeg is 8.5 deg against the film's 249.8 — the render's flames wash orange across most of the board and the whole kerb, whereas in the film a flame of the same size leaves the marble two squares away still cold blue-grey, its warmth confined to a pool under a metre wide. warmFraction 0.271 vs 0.175. Second, the veining is the wrong scale and the wrong statistics: the render puts three or four big smooth Calacatta swoops on an otherwise glassy-clean cream square, while the film's light squares are covered edge to edge in dense fine crackled mottling. That shows in the numbers — detailByBand high is 0.01197 against 0.02969, still 2.5x short, and gradientAnisotropy has regressed to 1.870 from round 3's 2.104 against the film's 2.682, meaning the added figure is isotropic blobs rather than directional stone grain.

history.gap: Marble field carries no figure — no dark branching veins on the light squares, no paler veining on the dark squares, and no inlaid geometric border strip; the floor plane is the lowest-detail region of the frame instead of the highest.

Light squares still carry no bold dark branching veins — only soft airbrushed smears — and have collapsed to nearly the same mid blue-grey value as the dark squares; the surface is matte with no reflections, and the inlaid border is a flat dashed marquee line on every joint instead of one carved band between field and kerb.

Veining and the cream/navy value split have landed, but every square joint is now a blown-white glowing hairline, turning the field into a wireframe grid; in the film the joints are the darkest thing on the board — recessed grooves carrying a fine dark beaded inlay — and no joint is ever brighter than the marble beside it.
